howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.introAfter: impose extra burden on upstream RSSHub instances or the original websites being crawled:

coalescing.title: Two-level request coalescing
coalescing.summary: — Concurrent requests for the same route first share the same Promise within a Worker isolate, so most duplicate traffic is merged there.
coalescing.cost: Durable Objects were originally used for cross-isolate coalescing, but the current cost is too high: they have triggered two $12.50 charges. After analysis, the extra benefit is small.
coalescing.current: Only about 1% of eligible requests currently attempt to enter the Durable Object; the rest use isolate-level coalescing and direct upstream forwarding.

cacheAware.title: Cache-aware routing
cacheAware.body: — Before making an actual request, the balancer checks all upstream instances in parallel to find one that has already cached the route. The request is then forwarded to the cached instance, which serves its cached content without re-crawling the source website.

noImpact.title: No impact on original websites
noImpact.body: — Each RSSHub instance maintains its own cache and crawl schedule. This balancer only distributes requests at the RSSHub instance level; it never crawls original websites directly, nor does it alter any instance's crawl frequency.
